title: GOES-13 proton flux during the 10 September 2017 storm
agency: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (partner agency)
dataset_id: GOES-13 EPEAD corrected integral proton flux, 5-min (g13_epead_cpflux_5m_20170901_20170930)
licence: U.S. Government work (no U.S. copyright); free to use with credit
citation: NOAA NCEI, GOES-13 SEM EPEAD corrected proton flux, September 2017.
fields_used: ZPGT10E (>10 MeV, east-facing, p/(cm^2 s sr))

derived.name: gt10MeV_reaches_10pfu
derived.formula: first 5-min value >= 10 pfu after the X8.2 flare

derived.name: storm_level_end
derived.formula: first valid 5-min ZPGT10E value < 10 pfu after the event peak
derived.drives: P-02 replay duration boundary (real storm continues beyond the chart)

derived.name: storm_shift1_mean_gt10MeV
derived.formula: mean ZPGT10E over [onset+0 h, onset+7.2 h)
derived.drives: historical 7.2-hour block 1; P-02 replays only blocks 1-2

derived.name: storm_shift2_mean_gt10MeV
derived.formula: mean ZPGT10E over [onset+7.2 h, onset+14.4 h)
derived.drives: historical 7.2-hour block 2; P-02 replays only blocks 1-2

derived.name: storm_shift3_mean_gt10MeV
derived.formula: mean ZPGT10E over [onset+14.4 h, onset+21.6 h)
derived.drives: historical 7.2-hour block 3; P-02 replays only blocks 1-2

derived.name: storm_shift4_mean_gt10MeV
derived.formula: mean ZPGT10E over [onset+21.6 h, onset+28.8 h)
derived.drives: historical 7.2-hour block 4; P-02 replays only blocks 1-2

boundary: Measured in geostationary orbit, about 36,000 km above Earth, where Earth's magnetic field barely slows protons this fast; a flux, not a dose at the Moon. East-facing detector; its 1,493.5 pfu peak at 11 Sep 11:45 UT agrees within 1% with NOAA's official 1,490 pfu event peak. The chart ends on 12 Sep while the storm continues until 14 Sep 17:25 UT; Aurora shortens this to two storm shifts as a game rule. pfu = protons/(cm^2 s sr).
